In the context of the Danish IBD quality database, a "Quality Target" (udviklingsmål) refers to specific clinical benchmarks designed to ensure high standards of care and monitoring for patients with [[IBD]]. These targets are established to track the quality of treatment and preventative measures across healthcare providers, ensuring that patients receive guideline-concordant care.

The registry defines precise thresholds for patient monitoring based on the specific treatments they receive. For instance, to mitigate the risk of osteoporosis in older patients receiving corticosteroids, a quality target (Indicator 4) mandates that at least 80% of steroid courses given to IBD patients over the age of 50 must be accompanied by a [[DEXA-scanning]] [^src1]. 

Similarly, for patients undergoing advanced therapies, the registry emphasizes the importance of regular disease activity monitoring. A specific target (Indicator 5) requires that at least 80% of patients being treated with [[Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (BMSL) must have their fecal [[calprotectin]] levels measured at least once a year [^src1]. These benchmarks ensure that patients on potent biologic or targeted synthetic therapies are routinely evaluated for intestinal inflammation and treatment efficacy.

## Claims
- Udviklingsmålet for Indikator 4 er, at mindst 80 % af steroidkure givet til patienter over 50 år med IBD skal have foretaget DEXA-scanning [^src1] (ibd, dexa-scanning)
  Type: quality-target
  Page: 21
  Source: wikis/rkkp-danibd/raw/DANIBD_2024.pdf, pages 21-25
- Udviklingsmålet for Indikator 5 er, at mindst 80 % af patienter i behandling med BMSL skal få målt F-calprotectin mindst én gang årligt [^src1] (bmsl, calprotectin)
  Type: quality-target
  Page: 21
  Source: wikis/rkkp-danibd/raw/DANIBD_2024.pdf, pages 21-25
